chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Following a strong lead alto and reading ahead
summary: A second tenor follows the lead alto and chord pattern, reading a bar or two ahead rather than note for note.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

Yeah. Certain alto players -- Willie Smith. See, Willie Smith and Jimmy and Hilton Jefferson and all those are different alto players. So those alto players (inaudible), they can just carry you -- They're so strong and so dominant, they can just -- you got to go, you got to go along with them, you know, just pull you through. Because after all, if you're playing second tenor, you know where the second part is -- got to lay one note, you know. Ain't but so many notes that you can get out. You can't play a -- How can you be playing a second part and jump over and play a fourth part. So the second part lays right in there where you are -- you know, where you start off at. You just follow that pattern of a chord, and you can read -- that helps you read. Then when you're playing, you just look -- try to read two or
three bars ahead. You know, you just try to see that much -- a bar or two ahead when you're playing, you know.
